english_paragraphs: On 10 April 1912 the opulent liner Titanic left Southampton on her maiden voyage. A 1911 trade journal had dubbed her and her sister ship "practically unsinkable". At about 11.40pm on 14 April she collided with an iceberg; by 2.20am she had vanished beneath the waves, and the death toll would surpass 1,500.

Folklore blames arrogance. Yet the Titanic was compliant with the law. Under 1894 rules, Britain's maritime regulator pegged lifeboat numbers to gross tonnage (volume, not weight) on a scale that topped out at 16 boats for 10,000 tons or more. At about 46,000 tons she carried 20, exceeding the requirement. Their capacity was 1,178, roughly half the 2,200 aboard: sufficient in law, inadequate at sea.

Within radio range, the steamer Californian kept an equally lawful routine. Her sole wireless operator, Cyril Evans, was on the payroll of the Marconi company; when he slept, so did the radio. Around 11.30pm he switched off his set. Hindsight may call that negligence, yet no rule obliged him to stay vigilant, so the Titanic's frantic distress calls went unheard there.

Between April and July 1912, inquiries in Washington and London heard testimony from survivors and the Californian's crew. That July, American legislation made round-the-clock radio watch compulsory. In January 1914 delegates of 13 nations signed the first Safety of Life at Sea convention, stipulating lifeboat seats for all, continuous radio watch, and an ice patrol. The First World War stalled the treaty; the patrol went ahead regardless.
The doomed liner sank within three hours. The outdated rules she sailed under had stayed afloat since 1894; it took her dead to discredit them.
chinese_paragraphs: 1912年4月10日，豪华邮轮泰坦尼克号驶离南安普敦，开始首航。1911年，一本行业期刊曾将它和姊妹船称为“几乎不会沉没的船”。4月14日晚约11时40分，它撞上一座冰山；到次日凌晨2时20分，船已沉入海中，最终遇难人数超过1500。
坊间说法将灾难归咎于傲慢。然而，泰坦尼克号符合当时的法律。根据1894年的规定，英国海事监管机构按总吨位确定救生艇数量；总吨位衡量的是容积，并非重量。这套分级标准的上限，是对1万总吨及以上的船只要求配备16艘救生艇。泰坦尼克号约4.6万总吨，带了20艘，超过法定要求。但这些艇只能容纳1178人，约为船上2200人的一半：法律上足够，海上救生却不足。
在无线电通信范围内，加州人号轮船的值班惯例同样没有违规。船上唯一的报务员西里尔·埃文斯受雇于马可尼公司；他一休息，电台也随之无人值守。晚上约11时30分，他关掉了设备。事后看来，这或许可称为疏忽，但当时没有规定要求他保持值守，因此泰坦尼克号急切的求救信号在加州人号上无人听到。
1912年4月至7月，华盛顿和伦敦的调查听取了幸存者和加州人号船员的证词。同年7月，美国立法强制要求全天候无线电值守。1914年1月，13个国家的代表签署首部《海上人命安全公约》，规定救生艇座位必须足够全员使用、电台连续值守，并开展冰情巡逻。第一次世界大战使公约搁置，冰情巡逻却仍然开展起来。
这艘在劫难逃的邮轮不到三小时就沉没了。它所遵循的过时规定，却自1894年起一直照常施行；直到船上众多生命逝去，这些规定才失去了公信力。

illustration_prompt:
Create a single publication-quality landscape 3:2 narrative illustration for an adult illustrated English-reading booklet. Finished standalone artwork, not a book mockup, not a collage of multiple unrelated panels. Sophisticated contemporary editorial gouache and watercolor, carefully controlled colored-pencil accents, velvety matte paint, subtle warm paper texture, soft natural daylight. Warm ivory paper dominates; subdued eucalyptus and sage greens structure the composition; restrained buttery lemon-yellow and dusty terracotta accents. Calm, comfortable, refined, credible drawing and natural anatomy. An airy coherent composition with one clear story focal point and at most two supporting details, generous breathing room at all edges and softly feathered painted edges into ivory. Detailed but uncluttered. Historically and scientifically appropriate objects, clothing and setting. Show the particular article's pivotal event or mechanism rather than a generic portrait or generic textbook symbols. Human figures treated with dignity; no grotesque caricature, no sensational violence or visible injuries. For disasters, emphasize the setting, evidence or human response without graphic suffering. For uncertain scientific claims, depict the observations and investigation without presenting debated mechanisms as proven. Absolutely no typography, captions, letters, numbers, logos, watermarks, diagram labels, fake writing or invented charts anywhere. Do not render invisible forces as literal magic. Avoid corporate vector icons, slick 3D rendering and childish cartoon style. High-quality, print-ready visual storytelling, matching a warm ivory-and-sage adult watercolor booklet.

Article 15, The Myth of the Unsinkable. Focus on the inadequate lifeboat provision aboard the Titanic in April 1912, a quiet human-response scene rather than a spectacular collision. From the ship's boat deck at night, a historically plausible open wooden lifeboat hangs on steel davits just outside the white railing, above a calm dark North Atlantic sea. A small group of passengers in dignified early-1910s coats and pale canvas life belts waits farther along the long cream-white deck, with two crewmen attending the boat. The luxury liner's scale and the single modest boat form the central visual relationship. Warm lamplight gently illuminates the wood against subdued sage-blue water, softened into abundant warm ivory paper at the margins. Natural restrained figures, accurate nautical proportions, no modern orange vests or motorboats. Do not show a collision, flames, bodies, graphic panic, or a radio operator aboard the wrong ship. No literal charts or numeric boat counts. Convey the article's question of legal provision versus actual rescue capacity without depicting the lifeboat law as the cause of the iceberg collision.
approved_summary: 1912年，号称几乎不沉的泰坦尼克号首航撞冰山，不足三小时沉没，逾1500人遇难。
旧规按总吨位（容积）定艇数，万吨以上只需16艇；它有20艇、1178座，仅够船上2200人约一半。
附近加州人号的唯一报务员关机休息并未违规，电台没听到求救；当时没有全天值守的强制规定。
1912年美国强制全天守听；1914年13国签约，要求全员救生艇座位、连续守听和冰情巡逻。
一战使公约搁置，冰情巡逻仍启动；沿用自1894年的旧规暴露出：合法配置，并不等于安全足够。
